chunks: From him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say about the sacrifices of the Christians?' He said, 'There is no harm in them.' I said, 'But they mention the Messiah upon them.' He said, 'They only meant God by the Messiah.'
ai.seo_question: Are the sacrifices of the Christians permissible according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) ruling that Christian sacrifices are permissible because their invocation of 'the Messiah' (Isa) is understood as referring to God, reflecting the Shia principle of interpreting polytheistic terms through the lens of monotheistic intent. This juristic nuance highlights the flexibility in *dhimmī* dietary laws, distinguishing between literal shirk and contextual theological reference. The ruling underscores the importance of understanding the specific theological context of the People of the Book when determining the permissibility of their food.
